references.text: The psalmist confesses that God knows his thoughts from afar. Jesus knew the Pharisees' thoughts, which demonstrates His divine omniscience.
The Lord searches all hearts and understands every thought of the mind. Jesus demonstrated this very divine ability by knowing the dialogues and intentions of the Pharisees.
The Lord searches the heart and tests the kidneys. Jesus' ability to know the thoughts of those around Him reflects this divine attribute.
Matthew's parallel account of the healing of the man with the withered hand on the Sabbath, where Jesus also challenges the Pharisees about whether it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.
Mark's parallel account of the healing of the man with the withered hand in the synagogue on the Sabbath, including Jesus' command for him to stand up in front of everyone.
Jesus knew what the scribes were thinking in their hearts, a parallel to how He here knew the thoughts and dialogues of the Pharisees.
Jesus knew the thoughts of the Pharisees. This confirms the pattern in the Gospels that Jesus had divine insight into people's inner mental lives.
Earlier in Luke, Jesus knew the thoughts of the Pharisees and scribes when they questioned His authority to forgive sins—the same pattern of knowing people's thoughts.
John testifies that Jesus knew all people and did not need anyone to testify about a person, for He Himself knew what was in man. This confirms Jesus' omniscience as shown in Luke 6:8.
Jesus refers to Himself as the one who searches kidneys and hearts, a divine attribute He demonstrated by knowing the thoughts of the Pharisees.
